about: page 2 $9400-$9DCC: the asteroid field ($9561-$9C19: set-up, launching, movement, view, collision with the player and the lazar test of the ten asteroid records), between two stretches that page 2 does not use - the end of an uncalled copy of S2VW ($9400-$9560) and, from $9C1A, a copy of page 0's wave data and of an IRQ routine

P2:9561.name: astrd_init
P2:9561.desc: set-up of the asteroid field, called by asteroid_setup (phase $48) when the asteroid part begins. puts objects $20-$22, the asteroid shapes, into the math box, presets the ten asteroid records ($17 bytes each, from ALIENZ up to MESBLK) from astrd_init_tab with random spin angles and leaves them all free, sets astrd_max from w4_level through astrd_max_tab (3 to 10) and clears the launch delay

P2:965E.name: astrd_man_init
P2:965E.desc: set-up of the asteroid pages of the training manual, called by man_init_asteroid with B = the manual page. takes entry B of astrd_man_tab (entry 0 for page 3 and up) and makes the first record one asteroid at rest $1000 ahead of the player with that entry's spin rates, frees the other nine records, puts objects $20-$22 into the math box and sets astrd_max to 0 so that nothing is launched

P2:96E0.name: astrd_move_all
P2:96E0.desc: one frame of the asteroid field, called by the asteroid phase ($2C), by the death in the field (phase $3C) and by the manual. counts the launch delay down and, when it is 0 and one of the first astrd_max records is free, launches an asteroid into it (astrd_launch) and takes the next delay from astrd_delay_tab by w4_level + diff_adder. when the field is stopped (astrd_max minus) it frees every asteroid that was not in view in the last frame. then spins and moves every record in use

P2:9782.name: astrd_spin
P2:9782.desc: turns the asteroid at U: adds the yaw rate (byte $13) to the yaw angle (byte $12) and the pitch rate (byte $15) to the pitch angle (byte $14)

P2:97A3.name: astrd_move_one
P2:97A3.desc: moves the asteroid at U: runs the hit flash timer (astrd_flash_tmr) and, if the record is still in use, calls the movement routine of its type (byte 4, 0-6) through astrd_move_tab. X is preserved

P2:97BC.name: astrd_flash_tmr
P2:97BC.desc: timer of the hit flash, byte 3 of the record at U: when it is running it goes down by 2 a frame, and when it runs out with status bit 5 or 4 set the record is freed

P2:97D0.name: astrd_mv_follow
P2:97D0.desc: movement type 0, reached through astrd_move_tab: only makes the position relative to the player (astrd_to_rel), so the asteroid keeps its place in front of the ship. astrd_hit_player gives this type to an asteroid that has hit, whose record then holds a screen position and is left alone

P2:97D4.name: astrd_mv_stay
P2:97D4.desc: movement type 1, reached through astrd_move_tab: only makes the position a universe position (astrd_to_univ), so the asteroid stays where it is and the player flies past. the type of the manual's asteroid

P2:97D8.name: astrd_mv_close
P2:97D8.desc: movement type 2, reached through astrd_move_tab: with the position relative to the player it takes a quarter off x and a sixteenth off y and z each frame, and changes to type 1 once x is under $1000. no instruction was found that gives a record this type

P2:980C.name: astrd_mv_home
P2:980C.desc: movement type 3, reached through astrd_move_tab: homes on the player. with the position relative to the player the velocity (words 12, 14, $10) becomes minus 1/32 of the position on each axis and is added, then the position is made a universe position again. when the y and z velocities are both $0200 or less in size the type becomes 4, straight flight with that velocity. only the preset of astrd_init gives this type, to records it leaves free

P2:986C.name: astrd_mv_home_y
P2:986C.desc: movement type 5, reached through astrd_move_tab: astrd_mv_home with the y velocity minus 1/16 of the y position instead of 1/32. one of the two types astrd_launch picks at random

P2:98CC.name: astrd_mv_home_z
P2:98CC.desc: movement type 6, reached through astrd_move_tab: astrd_mv_home with the z velocity minus 1/16 of the z position instead of 1/32. the other type astrd_launch picks

P2:992C.name: astrd_mv_straight
P2:992C.desc: movement type 4, reached through astrd_move_tab: makes the position a universe position and adds the velocity words 12, 14 and $10 to it, a straight flight with the velocity the homing types left

P2:9943.name: astrd_to_rel
P2:9943.desc: if the position of the asteroid at U is a universe position (status bit 6 set) it takes the player's position (s1_tx, s1_ty, s1_tz) off x, y and z and clears the bit: the position is now relative to the player

P2:9963.name: astrd_to_univ
P2:9963.desc: the reverse of astrd_to_rel: if the position of the asteroid at U is relative to the player (status bit 6 clear) it adds the player's position to x, y and z and sets the bit

P2:9983.name: astrd_view_all
P2:9983.desc: views the asteroid records, called with Y at the display list by the view routines of the asteroid phase (LA5F9), of the death in the field (LA66A) and of the manual (man_view_asteroid). for every record in use, with S2_PRM pointing at it: one that has hit the player (status bit 5) gets its flash drawn (astrd_flash_view), any other has its flags byte cleared and is viewed by astrd_view_one

P2:99A8.name: astrd_view_one
P2:99A8.desc: views the asteroid at U. its universe position goes through the math box (MS_PSB2 on the scratch block) to give its place in the player's view. it is freed when its distance ahead is $0100 or less or when it is outside the view to the side or above or below. otherwise flag bit 4 (in view) is set, the asteroid hits the player (astrd_hit_player) when its distance is no more than its own x speed plus the player's plus $0200, and it is drawn (astrd_draw)

P2:9A3A.name: astrd_draw
P2:9A3A.desc: draws the asteroid of S2_PRM at the place astrd_view_one left in M_XT, M_YT, M_ZT: fresh unit vectors in the ship 2 download block are yawed and pitched by the record's two angles and concatenated with the player's view (MS_CNCT), bank 1 projects the points of object $21, the lazar test astrd_lz_test is made, and the object is drawn in the colour of its size index

P2:9A8D.name: astrd_flash_view
P2:9A8D.desc: view of an asteroid that has hit the player: a blank vector from the screen centre to the screen position astrd_hit_player saved in words 6 and 8, then falls into astrd_flash_draw

P2:9A99.name: astrd_flash_draw
P2:9A99.desc: draws the hit flash at the beam's position: a scale instruction and a colour 7 instruction that both take their low byte from the flash timer (byte 3) times 16, then the picture whose JSRL is at index byte $16 of bank 0's table LB962, and bank 1 brings the beam back to the centre. entered from astrd_hit_player for the first frame and by falling in from astrd_flash_view after that

P2:9ABA.name: astrd_hit_player
P2:9ABA.desc: an asteroid at U has run into the player. bank 1 draws the vector to its centre and the y and x of that vector are saved in words 6 and 8 as the screen position of the flash, picture index 8, status bit 5 set (bits 6, 3 and 0 cleared), type 0, flash timer $0F. the ship starts to glow (BG1GLW, which costs a shield), the roll after a hit is cancelled, the shield and asteroid hit sounds are sent and the first frame of the flash is drawn

P2:9AFD.name: astrd_free
P2:9AFD.desc: frees the asteroid record at U: status and flags bytes 0

P2:9B04.name: astrd_launch
P2:9B04.desc: launches an asteroid into the free record at U: status $41 (in use, universe position), flags, flash timer and size index 0, movement type 5 or 6 by the sign of a random byte, a random yaw rate of 0-7 either way, and a second random value up to 7 either way stored in the pitch angle. the scratch point x $7000 with random y and z goes through the math box program MS_PSUB and the result becomes the record's position

P2:9B7A.name: astrd_oct_dist
P2:9B7A.desc: octagon distance from the screen point in M_YP (x) and M_ZP (y) to the lazar cursor LZ_CX, LZ_CY: the larger of the two absolute distances, or 9/16 of their sum if that is more, less 10 for the cursor, not below 0. result in D. uses the temps at $4801 and $4803. called by astrd_lz_test

P2:9BC3.name: astrd_lz_test
P2:9BC3.desc: lazar test of the asteroid being drawn (U = record, its view position in M_XT, M_YT, M_ZT), called by astrd_draw. skipped when the asteroid is not nearer than astr_hit_d. it projects the radius of the record's size index (astrd_size_tab) and the centre to the screen, and when the cursor's octagon distance to the centre is less than that radius it records the asteroid as the nearest under the cursor: astr_hit_d = its distance, astr_hit_rec = 0. X is preserved

P2:9C16.name: astrd_lz_hit
P2:9C16.desc: loads U from astr_hit_rec and returns. reached through the maze from page 3 (P3_98C9) when the lazar's nearest target is an asteroid whose astr_hit_rec is not 0 - which astrd_lz_test never makes it, so the lazar only splashes against an asteroid and this entry is not reached

4C68.name: astrd_delay
4C68.desc: asteroid field: frames until the next asteroid may be launched. astrd_init clears it, astrd_move_all counts it down to 0 and, after a launch, reloads it from astrd_delay_tab by w4_level + diff_adder (12 frames down to 2)

questions: P2:9400-9560 - the end of the copy of SNVW/S2VW that starts at P2_93D2. the tracer has it as an orphan, no maze entry of page 2 leads to it, and the bytes $9361-$9560 are the same on page 3 ($9472-$9560 on page 0, $952B-$9560 on page 1), so it looks like an older image that each page's own code was laid over. it is disassembled and carries Atari's comments, which is harmless, but it is not live code of page 2

P2:9C1A-9DCC (and on to $9E2C) - not a data block of page 2. $9C1B-$9CA6 equals page 0's TSPWAV wave data (page 0 has $00 at $9C1A where page 2 has $FF, the one byte I cannot place: it is not read by the code before it) and $9CA7 on is 6809 code, a copy of the IRQ routine located for this address whose JSRs go to $9EEA, $9EFD, $9F44 and $9FE2. nothing in page 2 refers to any of it: the only reference is the decoy maze entry P2_82FB JSR P2_9CF2, which lands in the middle of an instruction, and the tracer has $9EEA, $9EFD and $9F44 as orphans. so on this page nothing uses the tail's routines. the listing could show $9CA7-$9DCC as code, but as dead code it may be better left as bytes

P2:9861, P2:98C1, P2:9921 - CMPD #$0000 followed by BCC always branches, so the three homing types never change to type 1 there. it reads like a test for the asteroid having passed the player that does not work as written

P2:9B3B - astrd_launch stores its second random value in the pitch angle (byte $14) right after computing it like a rate, and never writes the pitch rate (byte $15), which keeps the value of astrd_init_tab. it may have been meant for $15

P2:9A62 - the object drawn is always $21 (LDB #$01 before the ANDB #$03), while the lazar test and the colour go by the size index in byte 5, which is 0 (radius 1000) for every launched asteroid and 1 for the manual's. objects $20 and $22 are put in the math box but not drawn by this code
movement types 2 and 3 (P2_97D8, P2_980C) are in astrd_move_tab but no instruction in this stretch gives a live record either type

4803, 4805 - shown bare in astrd_oct_dist and astrd_lz_test. they are the shared temps that already carry several of Atari's names (TMPOCT/TMPSIZ, TMPXD), so they are not named again here. 5098 is used as the player's x position and is named s1_tx by the page 0, 1 and 2 notes (p0_85ec, p1_8c00, p2_8a00), 4C15 and 4C17 are named astr_hit_d and astr_hit_rec by p3_9800: those names are used in the texts here and not given again
